text_blocks.snippet: Research suggests that moderate coffee consumption may be associated with a reduced risk of Alzheimer's disease, while excessive consumption might be linked to increased risk. Specifically, studies have indicated that drinking one to two cups of coffee daily is associated with a lower risk of cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease, compared to those who drink less. Conversely, some studies have shown that drinking six or more cups of boiled coffee daily may be associated with an increased risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.
